`null` when unknown.

participant.description: The player's participant in its world session. Unique within it.

x.description: World x in metres, to the centimetre: +x points right on the map.

y.description: Height in metres, to the centimetre.

z.description: World z in metres, to the centimetre: +z points down the map.

MapWorld.description: One world session: the server's view of one game client.

connection.description:
The server's control connection of this game client; one world
session each. Unique and ascending within a frame.

drivers.description: The players' cars driving in the world, by `participant`.

omitted.description:
Cars the server left out of this frame: no usable position, state
that could not be read, or beyond a bound.

persona_id.description: The player's persona: `persona_id` in `profile` for the same driver.

rivals.description:
Roaming rivals, by `id`: the car while the game drives it, otherwise
the server's simulation of the racer on the road network.

traffic_ring.description:
The radii the native traffic policy uses around each driver; `null`
without traffic or while it is off.

world_ms.description: Milliseconds since this world session started, when it was observed.

State.description: Session states, in the order a successful session passes through them.

oneOf.description: Reading the installation, preparing content and the account.
The server is ready and the game is starting (`start` only).
The installed EA activation helper shows a window; no timeout.
Routing applied (`start`) or the server is listening (`serve`).
A stop was requested; closing the game, then the server.
The session ended normally.
The session ended with an error; `message` says why.

Status.description:
`artifacts/launcher/<id>/status.json`: the supervisor's latest state.
Also the final record of `setup`, `serve` and `start` with `--json`.

action.description:
What the session was started as. `serve` hosts the server and may
start the game on request; `null` only in records written before
this field existed.

game_running.description:
Whether the session's game process is running: from its start until
it exits. With `action` `serve` this tells hosting from playing.
Always `false` for an interrupted session.

message.description: What the session is doing or why it ended, for a person to read.

utc.description:
When this state was recorded, UTC. Records written by the old
PowerShell launcher use a longer ISO 8601 form with an offset.

worker_pid.description:
Supervisor process ID when recorded. Process IDs may be reused after
the process exits; verify identity before acting on one.

TrafficRing.description:
Horizontal metres around each driver. Cars are created between `inner`
and a little more than `outer` ahead of where the driver will be in about
three seconds (a quarter of that to the sides), and kept while within
`outer` of the driver.

inner.description: Metres; cars are created beyond this.

outer.description: Metres; cars are kept within this.

description: One line of the event stream.

oneOf.description: The session directory was created and the supervisor is starting.

session_directory.description: `artifacts/launcher/<id>/` with this session's logs and records.

oneOf.description: A state change, exactly as written to `status.json`.

One line a child process wrote to standard error, without its line
ending. Lines longer than 16 KiB arrive in several events. When the
supervisor falls behind, a line saying output was skipped replaces
the dropped text; the session's log files keep everything up to
their 4 MiB bound.

Where the cars are in the server's world sessions, read-only, at
most four times a second while one runs, and only when the server
wrote a newer frame. A frame lists every world session; one with no
worlds means none is running (any markers go). World positions are
in metres: on the `map-images` map +x points right and +z points
down, and headings are degrees clockwise from up the map. Requires
the `map-feed` capability.

frame.description:
The server's frame number: one more for every frame it wrote,
so frames only move forward.

skipped.description:
Frames the server wrote since the previous `map-feed` event that
were not delivered: a newer one arrived before the supervisor's
next poll, or one could not be read.

oneOf.description: The last line: how the command ended.

exit_code.description: The process exit code; see the exit code table in `--help`.

message.description: Why the command failed; `null` on success.

status.description:
The session's final status; `null` when the command was refused
before the supervisor recorded one.

utc.description: When the event was written, UTC.
